slides.title: Learn the shape. Plan your essay.
slides.notes: Ask: what do you think this lesson is about? A blueprint is a plan for a building. An essay needs a plan too.

slides.title: Why is this lesson important?
slides.body:
• Every good essay follows the same shape.
  • A clear plan makes writing faster and easier.
  • Examiners reward organised essays.
slides.notes: Frame: structure is the roadmap for the whole essay.

slides.title: Pair Talk
slides.body:
What are the four parts of a question?

Which side did you choose? Tell your partner.

Opinion — Reason — Evidence
slides.notes: Recap lesson 1: Context, Opinion A, Opinion B, Your choice. Students restate their card position in one sentence.

slides.title: The model essay has four parts
slides.body:
IntroductionAsks the question. Hooks the reader.
Paragraph 2Argues for individual sports.
Paragraph 3Argues for team sports.
ConclusionGives the writer's opinion.
slides.notes: Page 133. Point at each paragraph of the model essay on the projector.

slides.title: Page 132, Exercise 1
slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 1

QuestionHow many paragraphs are there?
AnswerThere are four paragraphs.
ExplanationOne introduction, two body paragraphs, and one conclusion.
slides.notes: Read the model essay on page 133 first, then reveal the answer.

slides.title: Page 132, Exercise 1
slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 1

QuestionWhat is the function of each paragraph?
AnswerThe introduction asks the question. Paragraph 2 argues for individual sports. Paragraph 3 argues for team sports. The conclusion gives the writer's opinion.
ExplanationEach paragraph has one job. The essay argues both sides before it chooses.
slides.notes: Elicit the function of each paragraph before revealing.

slides.title: Page 132, Exercise 1
slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 1

QuestionWhat is the writer's overall opinion?
AnswerTeam sports are better for young people.
ExplanationThe conclusion says young people learn more from playing on a team.
slides.notes: The opinion comes at the end. It answers the question from the introduction.

slides.title: Page 132, Exercise 1
slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 1

QuestionWhat are the two meanings of "there is no 'I' in team"?
AnswerLiteral: the word team has no letter i. Real meaning: the team matters more than any one player.
ExplanationThe writer uses it to say teamwork is more valuable than individual success.
slides.notes: CCQ: is the writer talking about spelling, or about teamwork? Both.

slides.title: Strategy: Compare and contrast
slides.body:
DoPresent two ideas. Argue each in turn.
WhyThe reader sees both sides fairly.
HowEnd with your preference and why.
slides.notes: Page 132, Writing strategy. The model argues individual first, then team, then chooses.

slides.title: Page 132, Exercise 2 — Notes
slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 2 — Notes

TaskComplete the notes about team and individual sports.
1Team sports have to be organized with others.
2Individual success is more satisfying.
3Learning to cooperate with others is more valuable.
4Being part of a team can lead to arguments.
slides.notes: Read the essay again first. Reveal the completed notes row by row.

slides.title: Page 134, Exercise 4
slides.body:
Think of positives and negatives for both sides of your topic.

Write them in the table on your worksheet.
slides.notes: Pairs work together. Monitor: both aspects must have ideas in both columns.

slides.title: Strategy: Select and order
slides.body:
DoChoose the best ideas.
WhyYou have space for only three or four.
HowPick the strongest. Pick the clearest.
slides.notes: Page 134, Writing strategy. Students keep the best arguments, not all of them.

slides.title: Page 134, Exercise 6 — Expressions
slides.body:
Page 134, Exercise 6 — Expressions

TaskMatch the expressions.
1Let's start by looking at …= Let's begin with …
2Then there's the fact that …= Another point is that …
3In addition, …= Also, …
4What's more, …= Furthermore, …
5Finally, …= Last but not least, …
6To conclude, …= In conclusion, …
slides.notes: The left column is from the textbook list. The right column is the model's version. Students use these to introduce their own ideas.

slides.title: Page 134, Exercises 5 and 7
slides.body:
Choose your three best ideas.

Write sentences with the expressions from Exercise 6.
slides.notes: This planning output feeds lesson 3: drafting the essay.

slides.title: Your plan is ready
slides.body: You know the shape. You have a plan. Next lesson: we write the essay.
slides.notes: Collect the plans. Preview lesson 3: drafting introduction, body, and conclusion.
